title: Reconciliation Cycle and Sponsor Dispute Window on the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans
content:
Two periods, both counted in calendar days, are scheduled per plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans: the days between one reconciliation of the sponsor's roster against the plan's own enrollment records and the next, and the days a sponsor has to dispute a reconciliation finding.

| Group plan | Days between reconciliations | Days the sponsor has to dispute a finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Standard (PPO) | 90 | 30 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Enhanced (PPO) | 90 | 30 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Premium (PPO) | 30 | 45 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Standard (EGWP) | 90 | 30 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Enhanced (EGWP) | 90 | 30 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Premium (EGWP) | 30 | 45 |

## Points of judgement on the schedule

The two periods run in opposite directions across the book. Ridgecrest Group Retiree Premium (PPO) and Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Premium (EGWP) are reconciled most often, every 30 calendar days, and give the sponsor the longest dispute window, 45 calendar days. The other four plans of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans are reconciled every 90 calendar days and give the sponsor 30 calendar days to dispute.

On those two plans the dispute window is longer than the interval between reconciliations, so a finding may still be open for dispute when the next reconciliation falls due. On the other four the dispute window is shorter than the interval, by 60 calendar days.
